articles.title: Can the Boss’s Technology Dismantle the Boss’s Penthouse?A Case for Ecological Operaismo
articles.author: Socialist Forum
articles.content_excerpt: “The smarter our life, the less control we have over it.” —Jathan Sadowski [1] In a world where Big Tech too often sets the terms and conditions of basic human interaction within and beyond the workplace, more and more people are wondering how many of the supposedly “necessary” or “inevitable” algorithmic technologies we really need. Is it even possible for this digital machinery to serve the long-term interests of the many instead of the short-term interests of the few? For French Marxist philosopher and first-wave eco-socialist André Gorz, the answer, in many cases, was no. “It is only because capital needs consumers for its products that production also serves human needs,” he wrote. articles.title: One barricade after another: How protesters marched on the garrisoned heart of India’s capital
articles.author: Pavan Kulkarni
articles.content_excerpt: 60,000 security personnel were deployed across India’s national capital on October 10.​ This included the police of Delhi and neighboring states, as well as paramilitary forces pulled from regions of India affected by armed insurgencies. articles.title: South Africa anti-immigrant protests turns violent
articles.author: Nicholas Mwangi
articles.content_excerpt: Last week, anti-immigrant protests in South Africa turned violent, with looting, destruction of property, and reports of 24 vehicles being burnt as tensions escalated in Johannesburg and Durban. The unrest followed growing anger over a government directive on asylum applications, which the Department of Home Affairs has since withdrawn. The directive, issued on September 28, instructed Refugee Reception Offices (RROs) to process all asylum applications immediately. Massive queues of foreign nationals subsequently formed at immigration offices, which were met with demonstrations and violence from anti-immigrant groups. articles.title: China, BRICS & Brazil: what Lula vs. Bolsonaro means for the Global South
articles.author: Amanda Yee
articles.content_excerpt: As Brazil heads into the October 25 runoff election between President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Flávio Bolsonaro, the country stands as a crucial battleground in Washington’s strategy to contain China, as well as global geopolitics. What does this election mean for the future of China-Brazil ties, the BRICS alliance, and independent technological sovereignty across the Global South? Tings Chak – researcher, writer, and art director for the Tricontinental: Institute for Social Research – joins Amanda Yee to break down the two competing paths for Brazil represented by Lula and Bolsonaro. Read Chak’s article: “How Brazil’s election could reshape relations with China”

articles.title: In the crosshairs of AI (part two)
articles.author: Ashley Smith
articles.content_excerpt: I n their mad rush for profit and power, the tech oligarchs have unleashed artificial intelligence (AI) into nearly every corner of life on this planet. Firms are investing billions in data centers, which house the infrastructure to process the enormous amounts of information that power AI. They are also plowing ever more money into research and development. Their hope is that the technology will overcome global capitalism’s slump , which the system has been trapped in since the Great Recession, and trigger a new epoch of expansion. States are incorporating it into their police forces for domestic surveillance as well as their militaries for cyberwarfare and high-tech weapons. articles.title: Palestinian prisoner Dana Joudeh gave birth shackled to a bed, with a rifle pointed at her
articles.author: Aseel Saleh
articles.content_excerpt: When Dana Joudeh , 35, went into labor in mid-September, she was six months pregnant and being held at Israel’s Damon Prison. Her daughter, Lia, was born premature, and her family says she gave birth shackled to a bed, with a rifle pointed at her. Joudeh spent almost her entire pregnancy in Damon prison, held under a six-month administrative detention order. There she endured the conditions Palestinian prisoners have described since October 2023: medical neglect, inadequate healthcare, food deprivation, and sharp cuts to hygiene supplies. Read more: “We are here to kill you”: Released Palestinian prisoner exposes torture and medical neglect in Israeli prisons A day after giving birth, Dana and Lia were released from Damon Prison.
